attempts.docstring_words: Every top-level balanced object in the text is a candidate
attempts.code_does: It scans every occurrence of '{' not already covered by a previous raw_decode and decodes from there. This treats an object nested inside a top-level array as a candidate; with input [{"a":1}] it recovers the nested object {"a":1} even though the top-level value is an array, not an object.

attempts.docstring_words: Return None when the span is not in the document, else how it was matched ("verbatim" or a relaxation).
attempts.code_does: Normalizes whitespace in both span and document before checking, and returns "verbatim" if the normalized span is a substring of the normalized document, even when the original span is not literally present.

attempts.docstring_words: The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text
attempts.code_does: It only recognizes code fences whose opening fence is bare ```, ```json, or ```JSON (via _FENCE); a fence with any other tag such as ```python is ignored, so its object is treated only as a top-level candidate, and the function returns the last top-level object instead of the last fenced one.

attempts.docstring_words: The first refusal phrase the text contains, typographic quotes read as straight ones, or None.
attempts.code_does: Returns the first phrase in the refusal_phrases list that appears anywhere in the text, so it can return a phrase that is not the first refusal phrase occurring in the text.
attempts.example_input: refusal_phrase_in("I'm sorry, but I cannot", ("I cannot", "I'm sorry"))
